keyVerseText: Then stood up Jeshua the son of Jozadak, and his brethren the priests, and Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and his brethren, and builded the altar of the God of Israel, to offer burnt offerings thereon, as it is written in the law of Moses the man of God. Jeshua: also called, Joshua Zerubbabel: Gr. Zorobabel Shealtiel: Gr. Salathiel
rootMeaning: The name יוֹצָדָק (Yôwtsâdâq) is a Hebrew proper noun derived from the root יְהוֹצָדָק (Yᵉhôwtsâdâq), meaning "Jehovah is righteous." This etymology emphasizes God's righteousness as a defining attribute, rather than merely serving as a personal name. Understanding this root meaning enriches the common English transliteration by highlighting the theological declaration embedded in the name, affirming that the Lord's justice and uprightness underpin the identity of the individual named Jozadak.
usageInScripture: The term occurs five times in Scripture, consistently translated as "of Jozadak," indicating its use primarily as a patronymic reference. This consistency suggests the name functions chiefly to identify a historical figure connected to the priestly lineage rather than as a general noun or concept. The figure Jozadak is noted as the son of the high priest Seraiah and father of Joshua, anchoring his role within Israel's priestly heritage, even though he himself never served as high priest due to captivity.
theologicalSignificance: The name Jozadak, meaning "Jehovah is righteous," carries profound theological weight, especially given his priestly lineage and the historical context of exile. It reminds believers that God's righteousness remains steadfast even when His people face judgment and displacement. This truth encourages faith in God's just governance and His faithfulness to His covenant, despite human failure or national calamity. Moreover, as the father of Joshua the high priest who returned from exile, Jozadak's name foreshadows restoration grounded in divine righteousness, pointing ultimately to Christ as the perfect High Priest who embodies God's justice and mercy.
keyVerseReflection: Ezra 3:2 highlights Jeshua (Joshua), son of Jozadak, standing with the priests and Zerubbabel to rebuild the altar of God in Israel. The mention of Jozadak here situates Joshua within a priestly heritage defined by God's righteousness, linking the restoration efforts to a legacy of divine justice. This connection underscores the continuity of God's covenant faithfulness and the hope of renewal through obedient worship, even after exile and hardship.
